chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Do not sit with them, meaning the Murji'ah. May Allah curse them, and may Allah curse their sects, the Polytheists, who do not worship Allah upon anything of the things.

key_terms.الْمُرْجِئَةَ: The Murji'ah, a theological sect known for delaying judgment on sinners
key_terms.مِلَلَهُمُ: Their sects or schools of thought

ai.seo_question: Who are the Murji'ah and why are they cursed in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against socializing with the Murji'ah, a prominent early theological sect known for deferring judgment on major sins, by equating their spiritual deficiency with polytheism. He specifically curses their sects (milal) for failing to worship Allah with the requisite depth and correctness, highlighting the Shia emphasis on combining faith with righteous action. This serves as a practical guideline for maintaining doctrinal purity through selective companionship.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Al Nazar Bin Shuayb, from Aban Bin usman, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Do not gather with them, meaning the Murjiites. May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse them, and may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse their nation, the Polytheists who are not worshipping Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon anything from the things’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Muhammad ibn al- Husayn from al-Nadr ibn Shu’ayb from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Do not sit with them -al-Murji’a. May Allah condemn them! Allah has condemned their pagan nations which do not worship Allah on any good grounds.”
